headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: marker can’t write, while marketingskills can read/write and spawn subprocesses, making prompt injection and data leakage low but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker is document-processing with no filesystem read/write, shell, browser, subprocess, or MCP access, so it cannot directly ingest marketingskills outputs by default. marketingskills does read/write files and uses shared-context skills, so a manual or file-based bridge is plausible but unusual. The pathway exists, but blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies marketingskills output into a file that marker later processes, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced between the agents, marker may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste handoff of untrusted text.
Require a human review step before marker consumes marketing outputs.
Use file naming conventions that separate inputs from instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while marketingskills can read/write files and call allowlisted APIs. There is no documented shared workspace or shared principal, so leakage is not default. If the operator bridges them through files, marketingskills could expose content, but the blast radius is small and indirect.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, marketingskills can read marker-produced files.
IF marker outputs sensitive text into files that marketingskills uploads or summarizes, that content may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid placing sensitive documents in the shared path.
Restrict marketingskills API calls to non-sensitive inputs.
Review outbound requests before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker has no write or subprocess capability, but marketingskills can write files, read files, and spawn subprocesses, with multiple instances supported. If both are aimed at the same mutable workspace, marketingskills can overwrite or race on artifacts marker depends on. The conflict is plausible in default multi-agent setups, though marker itself cannot write.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory, marketingskills can clobber marker inputs or outputs.
IF multiple marketingskills instances run concurrently, file races become possible on shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Serialize writes to any shared folder.
Run only one marketingskills instance per workspace.
Use temporary files plus atomic renames.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is explicitly built around shared context and skills that build on each other, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream steps. marker produces document-processing outputs that marketingskills could reuse without a documented verification gate. That creates a plausible error-amplification chain, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes marker output without a verification step, errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on marketing drafts derived from marker output, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require source citations before reuse of marker output.
Limit marketingskills to drafting, not execution.
Flag low-confidence marker outputs for review.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between producer and consumer.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is documented for marker, while marketingskills touches marketing content and product marketing context. The pair shows no residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling gaps. The other agent is not cited because no regulated-data pathway is documented.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into the shared workflow, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF marketingskills is used on customer data with retention constraints, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention expectations for marketing artifacts.
Review vendor/data-processing terms before use.
Separate customer data from draft content.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing.
